principle: OS implements bounded, permission-checked generic WebSocket and audio codec capabilities. MiniApps implement application protocols such as XiaoZhi.

functions.name: passport.json.decode
functions.limits: depth <=8, <=256 values, string <=2048 bytes, reject duplicate keys and non-finite numbers

functions.name: passport.json.encode
functions.limits: depth <=8, <=256 values, output <=8192 bytes, string keys only, reject cycles and non-finite numbers

functions.name: passport.http.request
functions.limits: manifest domain allowlist, TLS verification, up to 8 app headers and 1024 aggregate header bytes, response <=8192 bytes; reject CR/LF, Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, and Connection headers

function.name: passport.system.public_device_identity
function.returns: device_id (stable board ID) and client_id (stable installation UUID)
function.description: User-approved, read-only identifiers for services that require device enrollment. Never returns eFuse secrets, private keys, Wi-Fi credentials, or arbitrary hardware data.

functions.name: passport.ws_connect
functions.limits: HTTPS/WSS, manifest domain allowlist, TLS verification, up to 4 app headers and 1024 aggregate header bytes; Host, Connection, Upgrade, and Sec-WebSocket-* headers rejected; CR/LF rejected

functions.name: passport.ws_send
functions.limits: bounded queued send; up to 50 messages/s and 16 KiB/s per session; bounded aggregate transfer and congestion handling

receive.fragmentation: OS reassembles protocol fragments into one bounded message; closes on message-size overflow or queue exhaustion

functions.name: passport.audio.capture_start
functions.description: OS captures from the board microphone and encodes bounded Opus frames. Raw PCM is never exposed to Lua.

functions.name: passport.audio.play_opus
functions.description: OS decodes and plays bounded frames through the board audio codec.

audio.lifecycle: capture, playback and queues stop on permission revocation, disconnect, app exit, or runtime fault

notes: The API v1 contract now lists the implemented runtime symbols and current limits. This historical draft is retained only as the design record; do not use it as the source of current API names or limits.
